subject: Clarify SOC 2 coverage: month inclusivity & snapshot timezone
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia@brightlineaudit.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
Cc: Greg Li <greg.li@acme-ml.com>, compliance@acme-ml.com
Date: 2026-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 time-range clarification for Acme intake

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question as we intake Redwood's SOC 2 Type II for Acme: the report cover page lists the period as 2025-07-01 through 2026-06-30. Acme's procurement team asked whether "June 30" should be interpreted as the entire day (i.e., inclusive through 23:59:59 local) or as a point-in-time cutoff (midnight UTC) for sampled evidence and logs.

Specifically: for any point-in-time evidence (e.g., access-control snapshots, config backups, system time-based log exports) does Redwood treat the final day of the period as inclusive in the customer's local timezone, or are those snapshots standardized to UTC and recorded at 00:00 UTC for audit sampling? Acme has a multi-region footprint and their legal team is being precise about timestamps because of retention cutoff rules in their contract.

Also, if you maintain any bridge letter or statement that clarifies inclusivity (EOD inclusive vs point-in-time) for the reporting period, can you share it? We can surface that to Acme's legal/procurement.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement hopes to finish their review this week.

Thanks,
Lydia
Lydia Park
Senior Auditor, BrightLine Audit
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
To: Lydia Park <lydia@brightlineaudit.com>, Greg Li <greg.li@acme-ml.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-08-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 time-range clarification for Acme intake

Hi Lydia, Greg —

Thanks for the note. Short answer: our SOC 2 report period is inclusive of the full calendar day for the stated end date when we provide monthly/per-interval evidence (so June 30 is inclusive through 23:59:59 in Redwood's primary logging timezone), but point-in-time artifacts are recorded in UTC by default. I'll explain the nuance below and attach the standard evidence matrix we share with customers.

Details:
- Monthly summaries & attestations: when we reference coverage for a given month (e.g., June 2026), it represents the entire calendar month (00:00:00 through 23:59:59) in the service's reporting timezone. For Redwood-hosted control evidence that is aggregated by month (backups, retention summaries), those are inclusive of the full day.
- Point-in-time samples (access-control dumps, KV cache snapshots, ephemeral token lists): our automation takes a timestamped snapshot in UTC (e.g., 2026-06-30T00:00:00Z) for reproducibility across regions. Auditors then map those UTC timestamps back to any local timezone if needed.
- Bridge letters: we do provide a bridge statement on request that clarifies this exact behavior; it specifically calls out that monthly inclusivity is based on Redwood's reporting timezone and that point-in-time exports are stored with UTC timestamps.

I'll attach the SOC 2 PDF and the point-in-time evidence matrix for Acme's review and can draft a short bridge letter if you'd like.

Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SOC 2 time-range clarification for Acme intake

Vanessa — thanks, that helps. A couple follow-ups from Procurement/Legal: can you confirm which timezone Redwood treats as the "service reporting timezone"? Acme operates primarily on PST for their US operations but they want to be explicit in the contract. Also, for the point-in-time artifacts, do you retain the raw export with the UTC timestamp, or is there any transformation (e.g., normalization to a canonical timezone) before archival?

If it's easier, a one-paragraph bridge letter we can append to the contract stating: (a) Redwood's reporting timezone; (b) monthly inclusivity semantics; and (c) UTC standardization for point-in-time export timestamps would be ideal.

—Greg
Head of Procurement, Acme ML
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
To: Greg Li <greg.li@acme-ml.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-08-24T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 time-range clarification for Acme intake

Hi Greg — quick answers from operations: 

1) Service reporting timezone: Redwood standardizes monthly reporting and retention summaries to Pacific Time (PT). We choose PT because our control-plane logs and S3 lifecycle jobs run in that timezone for billing and customer-facing reports. We will state "Pacific Time (UTC-7/UTC-8 depending on DST)" in the bridge to avoid ambiguity.

2) Point-in-time exports: raw exports are taken and stored with UTC timestamps (no timezone normalization applied to the timestamp field). Exports are archived to our secure bucket as-is and are retrievable with the original UTC timestamp.

3) Evidence retention: archived snapshots tied to the audit period are retained per the SOC evidence retention schedule in the attached matrix; we can produce the UTC-named export if Acme requests the raw file.

We can produce the one-paragraph bridge letter (Vanessa has final sign-off) and include the two supporting attachments referenced.

Neha Kapoor
Operations Manager, Trust Engineering
Redwood Inference

Greg, Lydia —

Per Neha's note, we've drafted the bridge statement and attached the SOC 2 PDF plus the point-in-time evidence matrix. The bridge paragraph reads: "Redwood's SOC 2 report period (e.g., 2025-07-01 through 2026-06-30) treats monthly coverage as inclusive of the full calendar day in Pacific Time (00:00:00 through 23:59:59 PT). Point-in-time artifacts captured for audit sampling are recorded and archived with Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) timestamps; raw exports are preserved with those UTC timestamps and can be provided on request."

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-07_to_2026-06.pdf (redacted public report) and point_in_time_evidence_matrix.xlsx (mapping of artifact type, storage key pattern, and timestamp conventions).

If Acme wants the actual raw export files for specific sampled timestamps, please tell us the object keys or the timestamp window and we'll pull them (SFTP or signed download link).
